images.filename: William S. Soule - Group at Camp Supply.jpg
images.caption:
Group at Camp Supply
This 1870 Soule photograph was taken in front of a typical sod house at Camp Supply. [...] This picture shows several army officers from the Third Infantry and Tenth Cavalry, together with sutlers, Arapaho Indians, and unidentified whites.— Smithsonian Instution, Bureau of American Ethnology. In: Wilbur Sturtevant Nye, Plains Indian raiders : the final phases of warfare from the Arkansas to the Red River, with original photographs by William S. Soule. University of Oklahoma Press, 1st edition, 1968, ISBN 0806111755, p392.

images.filename: William S. Soule - Issue day at Camp Supply.jpg
images.caption:
Issue day at Camp Supply
This is probably the first issue of rations and annuities at Camp Supply. For years this photograph was believed to have been made at Fort Sill, but more recent information places Camp Supply as the site. This identification comes from Morgan Otis, a construction engineer and a descendant of the Fort Marion Kiowa prisoner, Zotom (Zontam), and of Pacer, the Kiowa-Apache chief.[...] The agency ration issues initially were flour, sugar, coffee, dried fruit, and desiccated vegetables. Beef was issued later after the buffalo had become scarce.— Wilbur S. Nye collection, In: Wilbur Sturtevant Nye, Plains Indian raiders : the final phases of warfare from the Arkansas to the Red River, with original photographs by William S. Soule. University of Oklahoma Press, 1st edition, 1968, ISBN 0806111755, p352.

images.filename: William S. Soule - Powder Face and Family.jpg
images.caption:
Powder Face and Family
Arapaho man, Powder Face, breast ornaments of "hairpipes", Sitting on buffalo skin with wife and baby. Oklahoma, Camp Supply.

There was also a Cheyenne named Powder Face. The man shown in these photographs was identified by Ralph Whitetail-one of the oldest living Cheyennes-as being the Arapaho of that name.— Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology, In: Wilbur Sturtevant Nye, Plains Indian raiders : the final phases of warfare from the Arkansas to the Red River, with original photographs by William S. Soule. University of Oklahoma Press, 1st edition, 1968, ISBN 0806111755, p346.

images.filename: File-Three Cheyenne Chiefs Captured at the Battle of Washita , Taken at Camp -Fort- Supply, Indian Territory (2646b0d8d11042918927e1fc3126373e).tif
images.caption:
LIBI_00019_00395; This item is an original albumen photograph of 3 Cheyenne Indian chiefs (Fat Bear, Big Head and Dull Knife) captured at the Battle of Washita.  Dull Knife was not at the Battle of Washita.  The photograph is 4 3/4 x 7" (8 x 9 7/8" mounted) and was produced circa 1869 by W. S. Soule.  The image is believed to have been taken at Camp (Fort) Supply, Indian Territory.  On the front, a notation in Captain Frederick Benteen's handwriting reads, "Fat Bear/Big Head/Dull Knife/Cheyenne prisoners captured by 7th Cav--Comd. by..."  The remaining text has been cut off.  On the verso, a handwritten notation in pencil reads, "Three chiefs Autie captured in the Washita Campaign" and is signed by Elizabeth B. Custer.Note: "Pkg 6 Box 3" handwritten on the verso.  Photograph reprinted in "The Custer Album" by Lawrence A. Frost, page 104.; Print, Photographic [Mounted on Card]; Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National M
Keywords: little bighorn battlefield national monument
